_comment: Visual display constants. Edit freely to tune the look without touching code. See ui/knowledge.md for details on how each value is used.
_comment_target_fps: Render frame rate cap. Physics ticks are governed separately by gameplay.json ui.physics_tick_hz.

camera._comment: pixels_per_metre: zoom level. 9=1025x692 window, 12=1340x896, 14=1570x1032. margin_px: empty border around pitch. max_zoom/zoom_step: range and increment of the in-match ball-follow zoom control (the [-]/[+] control next to the sim-speed control, or Z to step) -- 1.0 is always the minimum (no zoom, whole pitch visible).

player._comment: min_radius_px: smallest on-screen circle radius drawn for a player. Physical world positions are unaffected — only the rendered dot size is boosted for visibility. inactive_alpha: opacity (0-255) of a player drawn translucent after being tackled (0=invisible, 255=fully opaque).

ball._comment: min_radius_px: smallest on-screen circle radius drawn for the ball. outline: whether to draw a dark border around the ball circle. outline_width_px: pixel width of that border (1=thin, 3=bold). height_boost_per_metre: how much the drawn ball radius grows per metre of height (0=no growth, 0.35=original exaggerated, 0.1=subtle).

action_icons._comment: linger_s: wall-clock seconds an action icon stays visible above a player after the action fires. font_size_px: point size of the icon font — keep small (10-14) or they'll dominate the screen.

speed_lines._comment: threshold_mps: player ground speed above which trailing speed lines are drawn behind the player. count: number of parallel lines. length_px: length of each line in pixels. gap_px: spacing between successive lines.

stamina_flash._comment: threshold: stamina fraction (0-1) below which a flashing warning outline pulses around the player. flash_hz: flashes per second (wall-clock).

heading_indicator._comment: A broad, thin 'V' of two lines touching the player's circle at wide-spread points and meeting just ahead in the facing direction — not filled. length_px: how far the meeting point extends beyond the circle edge. base_half_width_px: half the spread between the two rim contact points (bigger = broader V). base_inset_px: how far inside the rim the contact points sit (0 = exactly on the rim). alpha: 0=invisible, 255=fully opaque. Set alpha to 0 to hide entirely.

kick_ui._comment: Kick trajectory preview and spin input constants. max_drag_m: mouse distance (metres) for full power — also scales elevation and spin sensitivity. trajectory_duration_s: seconds of trajectory shown. max_loft_angle_deg: elevation at closest mouse position. max_spin_magnitude_rads: spin at furthest mouse position.

pause_notification._comment: font_size_px: point size of the auto-pause banner rendered when a human order completes. Default title_font is 32; 26 = ~20% smaller.

ball_spin_dots._comment: Dots on the 3D ball surface (Fibonacci sphere), always shown, rotating with ball spin. Only front-hemisphere dots (facing camera) are drawn — back hemisphere is hidden. count: number of dots. projection_scale_fraction: how wide the projected sphere appears relative to ball drawn radius (1.0 = dots reach ball edge). dot_radius_fraction: dot radius / ball drawn radius. color: RGB.

rings._comment: Opacity of EVERY ring: the players' selected / control-delay (cyan) / tackled (red) / low-stamina rings and the ball's state ring (blue airborne, green rolling, amber just bounced). 0-255; 0 hides them all, 255 is fully opaque. They are drawn UNDER the players and the ball, so a low alpha makes them a soft ground marking rather than an outline on top.

ball_state_rings._comment: Coloured indicator rings drawn around the ball to show its state. offset_px: how far outside the ball circle the ring sits. width_px: ring line width. Set show_flying/show_rolling/show_bounced to false to hide individual rings. Colors are [R,G,B]. bounce_duration_s: how long the amber bounce ring stays visible after a bounce (also controls physics.json just_bounced_display_duration_s if you want them in sync — but this one only affects the renderer display; to change the underlying timer duration edit physics.json). flying_min_height_above_ground_m: margin above ball.radius_m at which the flying ring activates (0.01 = only genuinely airborne).

pitch_markings._comment: Cosmetic pitch-line details (ui/renderer.py draw_pitch). spot_radius_m: centre spot and penalty spots (true-to-scale, with a 2px on-screen floor; the real mark is ~0.11m, bumped up so it reads next to the line width). penalty_arc_radius_m: radius of the arc outside each penalty box, centred on the penalty spot (Law 1: 9.15m). corner_arc_radius_m: quarter-circle at each corner (Law 1: 1m).

scene_light._comment: The one light used by every shadow and shading effect (ball shadow + shading, player shadows + shading): a point height_m above the middle of the pitch. Higher = shadows shorter and closer to their casters, shading more from above; lower = long sideways shadows near the edges.

player_shading._comment: Per-part rounded shading of the player sprites (shoulders, torso, head, limbs each lit as their own lump; dark on the side away from the scene light). strength 0-1; enabled false = the flat sprites.

player_shadow._comment: Ground shadow under each player, cast by the scene light (a figure's height h at distance d from the pitch centre throws a shadow d*h/(H-h) long straight away from the centre). alpha: 0-255 darkness. tip_fade: 0-0.9, how much lighter the shadow is at its tip than at the feet (like a real shadow it is also softer-edged toward the tip); 0 = uniform. contact_m: minimum shadow length in metres so a player at the centre still has one. enabled false = none.

ball_shadow._comment: Soft ground shadow under the ball, cast by the scene light (scene_light.height_m). A sphere's shadow is an ellipse: semi-minor axis the drawn ball's radius, semi-major radius/sin(light elevation), elongated away from the pitch centre and centred where the light through the ball's centre lands (distance*z/(H-z) beyond it). A grounded ball's shadow is a circle hidden under it at the centre that stretches and slides out with distance from it; a raised ball's lies further out. contact_radius_frac / contact_min_px: the MINIMUM contact shadow -- the ellipse is slid outward until its far tip clears the ball's edge by this fraction of the ball's drawn radius (so it scales with zoom exactly like the ball) or this many pixels, whichever is more; it fades out as the ball rises. 0 = none. alpha: 0-255 darkness of the shadow under a ball on the ground (fainter and softer as it rises).

ball_shading._comment: Sphere shading on the ball (dark on the side away from the light, clear where it faces it; the highlight is the unshaded part). The light is the scene light (scene_light.height_m above the pitch's middle), the same as the shadows, so the lit side always faces the centre: overhead at the centre, lower and more sideways toward the edges. strength 0-1; enabled false = flat white ball.

turf._comment: Grass texture instead of a flat green fill. patch_amp: +/- fraction of brightness of the soft, world-anchored light/dark patches (0 = none); patch_cell_m: size in metres of the big and small patch octaves; noise_amp: per-pixel grain (screen-space); vignette: darkening at the screen corners (0 = none); seed: the random seed. enabled false = the old flat fill.

goal_frame._comment: Slight 3D look for the goal frame in the top-down view (ui/renderer.py _draw_goal_frame). crossbar_lean_m: how far (world metres) the crossbar is drawn displaced from the goal line, away from the pitch -- a purely apparent parallax for its 2.44m height, clamped to the net depth; 0 = crossbar hidden exactly on the goal line (the old flat look). The net is drawn only behind the crossbar (the roof); the mouth in front of it is open. post_width_m: post/crossbar stroke width in world metres, but never less than 2px thicker than the net's own 1px lines (mesh and border), so the frame always reads heavier than the net. mouth_alpha: 0-255 tint over the goal mouth (the opening between goal line and crossbar); 0 = none. back_wall_alpha: the same tint over the back wall of the net (the strip between where the back of the net meets the ground and its top edge, displaced by the same lean); 0 = none. shade_strength: 0-1, how strongly the posts/crossbar are shaded to look round (lit from the top-left, see ui/style.py LIGHT_*); 0 = flat white.

corner_flag._comment: Corner flags (ui/renderer.py _draw_corner_flags), drawn with the same top-down parallax as the goal frame: the pole is vertical, so its top is displaced away from the pitch centre by pole_height_m * (crossbar_lean_m / goal_height_m) -- one parallax setting drives both. pole_height_m: APPARENT pole height for the parallax (a real corner pole is ~1.5-1.8m; this is deliberately bold so the leaning pole reads at the default zoom). pole_width_m: pole stroke (min 1px). flag_width_m: how far the cloth's free end streams off the pole (perpendicular to it, toward the pitch's middle along the touchline). flag_length_m: the cloth's length ALONG the pole in apparent metres (an absolute size, so a taller pole doesn't grow the pennant); the rest of the pole below it stays visible. shadow_alpha: 0-255 darkness of the flag's ground shadow (0 = none), cast by the scene light. shadow_height_m: the pole height used for that shadow. NOT the physical height: at a corner the scene light is only ~33 degrees above the horizon, so a 2.4m pole would throw a ~4m shadow (3.4x the drawn 1.2m pole stub); 1.2 gives ~1.9m. Raise it for a longer shadow.

goal_net._comment: Diagonal mesh drawn inside each goal frame. spacing_m: gap between mesh lines in world metres (smaller = denser mesh). min_spacing_px: floor on that gap in screen pixels -- below ~5px the 1px diagonals alias into a checkerboard instead of a diamond lattice (0.35m is only ~3px at the default window), so the gap never drops under this; lower it only if you want the checker back. back_spacing_scale: the back-wall net's mesh spacing as a multiple of the roof's (the steep back-wall lines in the narrow ~6px strip alias into a moire at 1x; 2x reads as clean tall diamonds). sag_m: how far (metres) the middle of the roof net hangs below crossbar height; the mesh bows toward the pitch by that height's parallax (0 = flat). alpha: 0=invisible, 255=fully opaque. color: RGB.

ball_trail._comment: Fading ghost trail behind moving ball. length: number of ghost positions stored (sampled at physics rate). min_speed_mps: no trail below this ground speed. max_alpha: alpha of the newest ghost position. radius_fraction: ghost circle radius relative to ball drawn radius. radius_taper: how much the radius shrinks toward the oldest ghost (0=no shrink, 0.35=oldest is 35% smaller than newest, 1.0=oldest shrinks to nothing). interp_steps: sub-samples inserted between each stored position when drawing (1=no interpolation, 3=two extra sub-points per gap).

player_sprites._comment: Top-down player sprite (head/shoulders/torso/limbs) drawn instead of a plain circle. Set enabled=false to fall back to the old circle rendering. size_scale: sprite's on-screen diameter as a multiple of the old circle's radius_px (bigger = larger sprite relative to the pitch). Colours are RGB triples: skin/hair/shorts/shoe/lace/stud (team shirt colour itself is TEAM_LEFT_COLOUR/TEAM_RIGHT_COLOUR in ui/style.py, not here). hair_coverage_deg: how much of the head (in degrees, out of 360) the hair patch covers, centred on the back of the head — 0 = bald, 360 = fully covered. Finer body-shape proportions (torso/limb/shoulder sizing) are intentionally not exposed here — they were tuned as an interdependent set; see ui/player_sprites.py to go further. Animation: top_speed_for_stride_mps is the pace (m/s) at which a player hits max_stride_hz (full strides/second) and full stride extension; below that, both stride rate and how far the stride extends scale down (so jogging shows a shorter, slower stride, not just a slower one) — extension_speed_exponent > 1 makes that extension drop-off steeper at low-to-mid speed (only nearing full extension close to top speed), 1.0 = linear, < 1 reaches full extension sooner.
